GoThru SSO Integration Guide

This guide explains how another GoThru application can integrate with GoThru SSO
using the same pattern used by Panorra PWA. The examples are language-neutral so
they can be applied to JavaScript, PHP, Go, Python, Java, mobile apps, or any
backend stack.

Flow Overview

The recommended integration is:

User opens your app
  -> frontend redirects to GoThru Keycloak login
  -> user signs in with GoThru
  -> frontend receives a Keycloak access token
  -> frontend sends that token to your backend
  -> backend verifies the token with Keycloak
  -> backend creates or finds the local app user
  -> backend returns your app session/JWT

The frontend proves that the browser login completed. The backend must verify
the token again before creating a local application session.

Keycloak Client Setup

Create one Keycloak client for each GoThru application.

For browser-based apps:

  • Client type: public
  • Client authentication: off
  • Standard flow: enabled
  • PKCE: S256
  • Valid redirect URI: https://your-app.example.com/callback
  • Web origin: https://your-app.example.com
  • Scopes: openid profile email

Do not put a Keycloak client secret in a frontend app. Browser and mobile apps
cannot keep a client secret private.

For server-side apps that exchange the authorization code on the backend:

  • Client type: confidential
  • Client authentication: on
  • Store KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET only on the backend
  • The frontend or browser should never receive the client secret

Frontend Contract

Every app needs these values:

GOTHRU_SSO_URL=https://id.gothru.org
GOTHRU_SSO_REALM=gothru
GOTHRU_SSO_CLIENT_ID=your-app-client-id
GOTHRU_SSO_REDIRECT_URI=https://your-app.example.com/callback

For development, use the dev Keycloak URL and the app's local callback URL:

GOTHRU_SSO_URL=https://gothru-sso.web.id
GOTHRU_SSO_REALM=gothru
GOTHRU_SSO_CLIENT_ID=your-app-client-id
GOTHRU_SSO_REDIRECT_URI=http://localhost:4200/callback

Frontend pseudocode:

create Keycloak/OIDC client with:
  url = GOTHRU_SSO_URL
  realm = GOTHRU_SSO_REALM
  clientId = GOTHRU_SSO_CLIENT_ID
  pkce = S256

redirect user to login

on callback:
  initialize OIDC client
  read access_token
  POST access_token to backend /auth/gothru
  receive local app session token
  store local app session using the app's normal session strategy

For Panorra PWA, this is implemented with keycloak-js and a /callback
route. Other frameworks can use their normal OIDC client library as long as they
use authorization code flow with PKCE.

Backend Contract

Every backend needs these values:

KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL=https://auth.gothru.co
KEYCLOAK_URL=https://auth.gothru.co
KEYCLOAK_REALM=gothru
KEYCLOAK_AUDIENCE=your-api-audience

For the current dev Keycloak server:

KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL=https://gothru-sso.web.id
KEYCLOAK_URL=https://gothru-sso.web.id
KEYCLOAK_REALM=gothru
KEYCLOAK_AUDIENCE=your-api-audience

KEYCLOAK_URL can be kept as a fallback alias for services that already read
that name. New services should prefer KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL.

Backend Login Endpoint

Expose a backend endpoint similar to Panorra's:

POST /auth/gothru
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "access_token": "<keycloak_access_token>"
}

Successful response should return the application's own session:

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "code": "success",
    "token": "<local_app_session_token>",
    "user": {
      "id": "local-user-id",
      "email": "user@example.com",
      "username": "username"
    }
  }
}

The local app token is not the Keycloak token. It is the token your own app uses
for API requests after login.

Backend Verification Options

Use one of these verification approaches.

Option A: Userinfo Verification

This is the simplest implementation and matches the current Panorra backend.

Backend pseudocode:

read access_token from request body
reject if missing

GET {KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL}/realms/{KEYCLOAK_REALM}/protocol/openid-connect/userinfo
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
Accept: application/json

if Keycloak returns 401 or 403:
  return 401 Unauthorized

if Keycloak returns non-2xx:
  return 502 Cannot verify GoThru token

read userinfo:
  sub
  email
  email_verified
  preferred_username
  name
  given_name
  family_name

find local user by keycloak sub
if not found:
  create or explicitly link local user

create local app session/JWT
return local app session/JWT

This works in any backend language because it is only an HTTP request to
Keycloak.

Option B: JWT/JWKS Verification

This is stronger and better for high-traffic APIs because the backend validates
the Keycloak JWT locally.

Backend requirements:

  • Fetch JWKS from:
    {KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL}/realms/{KEYCLOAK_REALM}/protocol/openid-connect/certs
  • Cache signing keys
  • Validate RS256 only
  • Validate issuer:
    {KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL}/realms/{KEYCLOAK_REALM}
  • Validate expiry
  • Validate audience when your Keycloak client is configured to include it
  • Use sub as the stable external user ID

Do not trust decoded JWT claims before signature validation succeeds.

User Mapping

Every app should store a link between the local user and Keycloak:

local_user_id
keycloak_sub
keycloak_email
keycloak_username
realm_name
linked_at

Use keycloak_sub as the stable identity. Email and username can change, so
they should not be the permanent link.

Recommended behavior:

  • Existing linked user: log in normally
  • New GoThru user: create local user or start onboarding
  • Existing local user with same verified email: link only if the product has
    approved this behavior
  • Unverified email: do not silently link accounts by email

Error Handling

Return safe, generic errors to the frontend:

Missing token -> 400
Invalid or expired token -> 401
Token verified, but local user is blocked -> 403
Backend cannot reach Keycloak -> 502
Unexpected app failure -> 500

Useful troubleshooting:

  • unauthorized_client: Keycloak client is probably confidential, has wrong
    redirect URI, or has invalid client settings for a public SPA.
  • Invalid client or Invalid client credentials: frontend is using a public
    flow against a client that requires a secret.
  • Cannot verify GoThru token: backend cannot verify the token with Keycloak.
    Check KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL, KEYCLOAK_REALM, network access, and token expiry.
  • aud is account: the token is valid for Keycloak account APIs. Configure an
    audience mapper if your backend validates a custom API audience.

Security Checklist

  • Use HTTPS in production.
  • Use authorization code flow with PKCE for browser/mobile apps.
  • Never store a Keycloak client secret in frontend code.
  • Treat access tokens like passwords. Do not paste them into tickets, chats, or
    logs.
  • Verify the token on the backend before creating an app session.
  • Use sub as the permanent external identity.
  • Validate token expiry.
  • Prefer JWKS validation for production APIs when possible.
  • Log diagnostic errors without logging full tokens or authorization headers.
  • Keep app session lifetime independent from the Keycloak access token lifetime.

Panorra Reference

Panorra PWA uses this pattern:

Angular callback route
  -> keycloak-js obtains Keycloak access token
  -> POST /auth/keycloak to app2-dev.panorra.com or app2.panorra.com
  -> Go backend calls Keycloak userinfo
  -> backend creates Panorra JWT
  -> frontend stores Panorra session

Other GoThru apps can keep the same contract while replacing Angular, Go, or
Fiber with their own framework.
